title: The Negotiator's Dilemma (Share vs. Guard)
description: The tension between sharing information to find joint gains and hiding it to avoid being exploited.

sections.title: What It Is
sections.content: The tension between sharing information to find joint gains and hiding it to avoid being exploited.

sections.title: How It Actually Appears
content: You want to reveal a flexible delivery date to get a better price, but you fear they'll use it against you.
In a partnership, you'd like to disclose future growth plans, but you worry they'll demand more equity.

sections.title: Typical Behaviors
content: Over-sharers reveal their full budget or deadlines early, then get squeezed.
Over-guarders reveal nothing, so no integrative trades are discovered.

sections.title: Tactical Approach
sections.content: Share interests, not positions. 'We're very focused on payment terms' (interest) instead of 'We must have net-60' (position). This keeps flexibility while testing their cooperation.

sections.title: Warning Sign of Exploitation
sections.content: They take your revealed interest and immediately convert it into a demand without any reciprocal sharing. For example, you mention needing speed; they respond, 'If you want it fast, that will cost an extra 20%.'

sections.title: Protection Strategy
sections.content: Give small signals of cooperation and see if they reciprocate. If not, tighten information flow.

sections.title: Key Insight
sections.content: Be conditionally open. Give a piece of information, then wait to see whether they give one back.
